help_panel_body.text:
• Enter the IP where the WebSocket Proxy Script is running.
• It may differ from the game server IP.
• 127.0.0.1 if running on the same PC,
• 192.168.(...) on local network (set static IP in router),
• External IP requires port forwarding.
• Enter the port configured in the WebSocket Script.
• Enter the token configured in the WebSocket Script.
help_panel_body.context: Help text explaining WebSocket connection. Preserve line breaks \n and bullet markers •.

help_telnet_title.text: Connect script to the game server

help_telnet_body.text:
• Enter the game server IP the script should connect to.
• 127.0.0.1 (localhost) if on the same machine,
• 192.168.(...) on local network (set static IP in router),
• External IP requires port forwarding.
• Check serverconfig.xml or sdtdserver.xml on your server.
• Ensure TelnetEnabled is set to true.
• Configure TelnetPort and TelnetPassword.
• Use a long password with letters, numbers, and symbols.
• This is the Telnet password, not the web control panel password.
help_telnet_body.context: Help text explaining 7 Days to Die Telnet setup. Keep XML filenames and TelnetEnabled, TelnetPort, TelnetPassword intact.

label_telnet_port.context: Short label for Telnet port input.

help_ws_body.text:
• IP address the SCRIPT should bind/listen to (not the game server).
• 127.0.0.1 (localhost) if running on the same PC,
• Specific local or external IP to restrict access,
• 0.0.0.0 to accept connections from any internal or external IP.
• External IP requires port forwarding.
• This is not the IP you enter in the panel connection tab.
• In the panel tab, point to the script's IP.
• WS Port (e.g., 8082) may require port forwarding.
• Create an authentication Token for the connection.
• Use a long password with letters, numbers, and symbols.
help_ws_body.context: Help text explaining Python WebSocket host and port. Preserve line breaks \n.

label_ws_listen.text: Allowed WS bind hosts (0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, or static)

help_bat_title.text: Generate .BAT file to launch the script
help_bat_title.context: Help dialog title for the .BAT file.

help_bat_body.text:
• The .BAT file is a shortcut to start the Python script.
• By default, it looks for the script in the same folder as the .BAT.
• If the script is in another folder, check the box and enter its path.
• The Python filename must match the file you saved.
• Example filename: WebsocketsExample.py
• The .BAT lets you start the bridge without opening a terminal.
help_bat_body.context: Help text explaining the Windows .BAT launcher. Keep WebsocketsExample.py and line breaks \n.

help_websync_body.text:
• Automatically sends player list and online counters every 5 minutes to a free cloud endpoint (e.g., Firebase Realtime Database).
• Your website reads this JSON directly via the visitor's browser.
• Even if the server or app closes, the latest count stays saved in the cloud.
help_websync_body.context: Help text for HTTP sync. Keep \n and •.
